classification.difficultyReason: Model an overtaking situation using literal speeds and an initial separation, solve for the common elapsed time, then calculate the requested distance.

content.prompt:
Jonathan is $c$ km due west of Anna when they start simultaneously walking in an easterly direction. Jonathan walks at a constant rate of $p$ km/h and Anna walks at a constant rate of $q$ km/h. How far will Jonathan have walked when he overtakes Anna?

(Assume that $p>q$.)

answer.short:
$\dfrac{cp}{p-q}$ km.

Equate Jonathan’s distance to Anna’s distance plus their initial separation.
answer.worked:
Let $t$ hours be the time until Jonathan overtakes Anna. Jonathan walks $pt$ km and Anna walks $qt$ km. Jonathan must cover $c$ km more than Anna.

$$\begin{align*}pt&=qt+c\\pt-qt&=c\\(p-q)t&=c\\t&=\frac{c}{p-q}\end{align*}$$

Jonathan’s distance is

$$\begin{align*}pt&=p\times\frac{c}{p-q}\\pt&=\frac{cp}{p-q}\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
